question: Shared: prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI from baseline data. Both models are multimodal and share the clinical/cognitive channel, which drives much of each model's performance. P-81 finds cognitive scores predict better than PET, and P-211 fits cognitive test scores in its Comb (a) and (b). The imaging channel differs: whole-brain FDG-PET in P-81, FreeSurfer structural MRI measures in P-211. Condition 1 is therefore met only through the shared cognitive channel. Horizons differ: 3 years in P-81; 1-5 years in P-211, with the recorded 0.92 at 5 years.

figures.P-81: Conversion within 3 years, FDG-PET + age + cognitive scores: AUC 0.7849 +/- 0.0963 (mean +/- fold SD, 5-fold CV validation sets; Table 3), 257 MCI (93 converters/164 stable). Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.7849/1.2151 = 0.6460; Q2 = 2(0.7849^2)/1.7849 = 0.6903; SE = 0.0314; 95% CI 0.723-0.846. Cognitive scores alone: AUC 0.7496 +/- 0.0683.
figures.P-211: Recorded: 5-year Comb (a), AUC 0.92 (225 participants at 5 years: 140 MCI/85 dementia). Hanley-McNeil over 85/140: SE 0.0214, CI 0.878-0.962. Matched 3-year figure (test data, Comb a): AUC 0.81 with interaction effects, 0.78 without. The 3-year cohort is 580 (392 MCI/188 dementia). Hanley-McNeil for 0.81 over a 10% test set (about 19/39): SE 0.0659, CI 0.681-0.939; over the whole 3-year cohort (188/392): SE 0.0207, CI 0.769-0.851.

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists and reconciles the pair. At P-81's 3-year horizon, P-211 prints test AUC 0.81 (0.78 without interaction effects). Both lie inside P-81's interval (0.723-0.846). P-81's 0.785 lies inside P-211's 3-year interval under either evaluation-set assumption (0.681-0.939 or 0.769-0.851). The headline gap (0.92 vs 0.785) is beyond uncertainty in both directions, but it sets a 5-year AUC against a 3-year one. P-211 itself shows its AUC is lowest at 3 years.
performance_validity: Not triggered for the compared figures: 0.785, 0.81 and 0.92 are all below 0.97. P-81's AD-vs-CN pre-training models with cognitive scores reached 1.000, which the authors attribute to circularity, but those are not the conversion figures compared.
reason: Both papers predict MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI and report AUC, sharing the cognitive channel while their imaging channels differ (PET vs MRI). The recorded gap sets P-211's 5-year AUC against P-81's 3-year AUC. At the matched 3-year horizon P-211 prints AUC 0.81, which agrees with P-81's 0.785 in both directions, so the papers' own figures dissolve the gap and condition 3 fails.

quotes.quote: the best model was a combination of FDG-PET, age, and neurocognitive data, yielding an AUC of 0.785 +/- 0.096 and a balanced accuracy of 0.733 +/- 0.098.
Balanced accuracy (BA), specificity, sensitivity, and AUC of the validation sets were obtained using 5-fold cross validation. Values shown are mean +/- standard deviation.
ii) neurocognitive scores predict better than PET per se
The five-years prediction accuracy reached 85% (AUC = 0.92) using both cognitive scores and MRI markers.

The mean AUC using Comb (a) displayed a characteristic pattern of first at about 0.9, then decreasing, reaching a low point at 3 years, followed by a gradual increase until 5 years of follow-up, to about 0.92.

The main performance indicators, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects) compared to 0.72, 0.76, 0.68, and 0.78 (without interaction effects), respectively.
Comb. (b) Cognitive test scores, plus age, gender, education, diagnose at baseline, and APOE4.
